summary: Har Dayal (1884–1939) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Delhi and at SOAS University of London around 1927–1932.

Har Dutt Sharma (d. 1942) was an Indologist who completed his doctoral studies under Moriz Winternitz. He served as Reader in Sanskrit at the University of Delhi and held a post at Hindu College, Delhi (attested 1957).

Hara Prasad Sastri (1853–1931) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (attested 1905) and as Joint Philological Secretary at The Asiatic Society (attested 1905–1911).
Harabhatta Sastri was an Indologist who held positions at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir, serving as a pandit in 1918 and attested there in 1922 and 1945.
Harabhatha Shastri was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir, where he is attested in 1911 and as a pandit in 1916.

Harald Christian Rasmussen (1853–1904) was an Indologist who studied under Michael Viggo Fausbøll at the University of Copenhagen (kand.theol. 1877, Ph.D. 1892). He served at De forenede Kirkeskoler as schoolteacher (1875), Senior Teacher (1882), and Skoleinspektør (1889).

Harald Hauptmann (1936–2018) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Tübingen, Saarland, Heidelberg (Promotion 1964), and FU Berlin (Habilitation 1978). He held posts at DAI, FU Berlin, Heidelberg, and DAI Istanbul.

Harald Hundius (1939–2019) worked in Buddhist studies and linguistics, studying under Singkha Wannasai around 1971–1980. He served as a lecturer at Chiang Mai University (1983) and as a professor at the University of Passau (~1993–2004).
Harald Wiese works in Indology and other fields. He earned his Dr. habil. at the University of Leipzig, where he became a professor in 1994.

Haraprasad Shastri (1853–1931) was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. Educated at Presidency University, Sanskrit College, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, he held posts at Sanskrit College, Presidency University, University of Dhaka, and Bangiya Sahitya Parishad.

Hari Damodar Velankar (1898–1967) was an Indologist who studied under Hari Mahadev Bhadkamkar. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Wilson College, Mumbai (attested 1944–1948) and as Joint Director at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan (attested 1959–1960).
Hari Pratap Kailash is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He studied at AIIMS New Delhi (MBBS 2000–2005), Jawaharlal Nehru University (MA 2008–2010), and the University of Delhi (PhD 2010–2015).

Hari Shankar Prasad works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and under Ramakant Tripathi, and completed his doctoral work under Jan Willem de Jong (attested 1982).

Haridas Bhattacharyya (1891–1956) worked in philosophy and religious studies. Educated at Scottish Church College and the University of Calcutta, he taught at Scottish Church College (1915), the University of Calcutta (1917), University of Dhaka (1921), and Banaras Hindu University (1947).
Harikrishna Sharma K. N. specializes in Indology and philosophy. He served as an Assistant Professor at V.T.B. College from 2011 to 2012 and at Sree Sankara College in 2012.

Harish Chandra Gupta worked in Indology and Tibetology and was attested at the National Library of India in 1970. He also held various engineering, environmental, and academic appointments between 2000 and 2024 after graduating from Government College Sanjauli.
Harish Chandra Mani Tripathi is an Indologist who studied under Karunapati Tripathi. He served as Publication Officer at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1996).

Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani (1917–2001) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Samaldas Arts College, Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, and under Muni Jinvijaya. He held posts at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, Gujarat University, and the L.D. Institute of Indology.

Harjot Oberoi specializes in religious studies, history and archaeology, and Indology. He studied at St. Stephen's College, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the Australian National University, and was appointed to a chair at the University of British Columbia around 1987.
Harogadde Manappa Nayak (1931–2000) worked in linguistics and Indology. He served as Director at the University of Mysore (~1961–1984) and as Vice-chancellor of Gulbarga University (1984–1987).
